sb_prompt: SEE HOW THE OTHER CALLER FEELS ABOUT THE PROPOSAL THAT ALL YOUNG AMERICANS SHOULD SPEND A YEAR OR TWO DOING SOME KIND OF PUBLIC SERVICE
turns: Hey, how's it going? You're the bus driver, right? I'm a manager at a grocery store. So, I was wondering, what do you think about this whole idea of young folks doing a year or two of public service?
Yeah, I mean, I've been driving the same route for six years, just figuring life out myself, but honestly, I'm kinda skeptical about forcing kids into it.
Yeah, I get that, but I've been thinking about this for years now, honestly can't really pinpoint why exactly I feel that way.
Yeah, it's just that when you're stuck in the same routine for six years, you start to feel like you don't really have much left to give to anyone else.
That makes sense, I mean, I've got the degree and the store to run, so I always felt like I had to give back somewhere before I just... stopped caring.

I mean, you could say I'm stuck, but I've seen these kids on my bus who don't have any idea what they're supposed to give, and it actually makes me wonder if a little structure wouldn't help them find something to give back.
True, but I still feel like we're just plugging holes in a leaky boat instead of teaching them how to build a new one themselves.

I guess the kids on my bus are already figuring out their own paths, but I'm still not sure if a year of mandatory service would actually help or just hold them back from the things they need right now.
Look, maybe it's because I've seen too many people use that time just to work cheap labor and say it's "service," so I just don't trust the whole idea anymore.
Yeah, I guess I do see that side too, but sometimes I feel like those kids would appreciate the structure more than I do.
I mean, it's like trying to fix a flat tire with a band-aid, nobody really wants to do it but they say they do, and then you're just stuck there looking at the same broken stuff over and over.
That's the thing though, nobody wants to do it, so if you make it mandatory, aren't you just forcing them to hate it right from the start?
I mean, if it's forced, how do you really know it's service and not just another year of them sitting around waiting for someone else to do the heavy lifting?
Yeah, but if they're not forced, who's going to show up to do the work that nobody else wants to do?
You make a good point, but I guess if they're just there waiting for someone else to do the work, they're not really doing the work themselves.
That's fair, but I'm starting to think maybe the mandate is just the only way to get enough bodies in the rooms that nobody else is filling.
Yeah, but if they're just there waiting for someone else to do the work, they're not really doing the work themselves.
I guess that's the risk, but if they don't show up at all, then we're just back to square one.
So it comes down to this: do we mandate it just to fill empty chairs, or do we trust that if they *have* to show up, they'll actually get off their butts and do something real?
I guess if they're just sitting there waiting, who's gonna pick up the heavy stuff when no one else shows up?
I mean, if you force them to sit in a chair, are they learning anything or just burning time waiting for a teacher to find them?
Yeah, but forcing them there isn't the same as making them care, and if they don't care, they'll probably just burn through the time without learning anything useful.
Yeah, but if they're just forced to sit there, they might burn out before they even learn what it means to show up.
Yeah, but forcing them to sit there might just make them resent the whole idea before they ever get a chance to actually do anything useful.
Yeah, but if they're just resenting the whole thing from the start, are they ever going to learn how to actually care about anything?
I guess if they're just resenting it from the start, they might as well go home and watch TV instead of wasting our money.
Right, but if they're just resenting it from the start, are they ever going to learn how to actually care about anything?
Yeah, but if they're just burning through the time resenting it, then who's actually going to learn how to care about anything?
Yeah, but if they're just resenting it from the start, are they ever going to learn how to actually care about anything?
I mean, nobody's gonna learn to care if they're just resenting the whole thing from day one.
So if nobody learns to care, then what exactly is the point of making them sit there at all?
But if nobody actually cares, then who's gonna pick up the heavy stuff when no one else shows up?
So if nobody picks up the heavy stuff, then what's the point of all this talk anyway?
So if we just make them sit there, we're wasting money and making them hate it, but if we don't make them sit there, nobody's gonna do the work at all.
So if nobody picks up the heavy stuff, we're just stuck paying for empty seats and angry kids for nothing.
Yeah, but if we don't make them sit there, who's gonna show up to do the work nobody else wants?
So we're just spinning our wheels here, aren't we?
Exactly, so we're just spinning our wheels here, are we?
It sounds like we're both just stuck in a loop, huh?
Yeah, looks like we're just going in circles, huh?
